children.text: Welcome to the second edition of Mathazine, “Mathematics for Plumheads”, our mathematics newsletter.

This edition explores the life and work of Al-Khwarizmi, the Father of Algebra, announces the Math Door Challenge for Grades 9–12, and explains dyscalculia and how it can affect everyday life. It also looks back at the soft launch event and includes a Sudoku puzzle, a comic, fun facts and math jokes.

children.text: In Grades 3 and 4, our teaching and learning approaches evolve to build upon the foundational skills acquired in the early years while further developing critical thinking, problem-solving, and collaboration skills.

heading.title: Building Strong Foundations for Deeper Learning

children.text: Teachers employ a balanced approach that combines teacher-led instruction with opportunities for inquiry-based learning and project-based tasks. The curriculum is designed to promote interdisciplinary connections, allowing students to make meaningful connections across subject areas. Through a combination of whole class instruction, small group activities, and independent inquiry, students in Grades 3 and 4 engage in deeper exploration of concepts and develop essential skills for academic success and lifelong learning.

Upper Elementary (Grades 3–5): The curriculum engages the students in interdisciplinary learning, and a noticeable emphasis is placed on collaboration, curiosity, and real-world applications. Technology integration becomes an integral part of the curriculum.

image.alt: SAIS - Dubai elementary students playing chess

children.text: In Grades 1 and 2, we are implementing an ongoing assessment model designed to provide a comprehensive and holistic view of each student’s progress. This shift moves away from solely relying on periodic tests and instead focuses on continuous evaluation through observations, classwork, homework, projects, discussions, and quizzes. This approach enables teachers to better understand and support students’ development throughout the year in a relaxed and stress-free environment.

While multiple formative and summative assessments will take place across subjects, parents will not be informed prior to their administration, to ensure assessments reflect authentic learning and reduce performance anxiety. However, in response to parent feedback and to support home preparation, schedules will be shared in advance for Arabic and Islamic Studies assessments only.

We continue using our proficiency scale for grades 1 and 2 to better reflect the progress and achievements of our students. We do convert these proficiency scales into percentages for our internal data analyses.

children.text: Arabic Language Curriculum
Motto:
“I Read with Understanding… Write with Creativity… and Express Myself with Confidence.”
For Arab Students:

The curriculum focuses on developing fluent reading, accurate writing, and confident self-expression. It encourages students to communicate their ideas effectively while strengthening independent learning, comprehension, and critical thinking skills.
For Non-Arab Students:

The curriculum follows a progressive approach to developing reading, writing, and speaking skills. It emphasizes building essential vocabulary and a solid foundation in Arabic grammar, enabling students to communicate effectively and confidently in various everyday situations.
Islamic Education Curriculum
For Arab Students:

The curriculum focuses on strengthening students’ understanding of the Holy Quran, the Sunnah of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), Islamic beliefs, and acts of worship. It connects Islamic teachings with moral values and authentic Emirati customs and traditions, encouraging students to apply these principles in their daily lives.
For Non-Arab Students:

The curriculum introduces fundamental Islamic concepts through accessible and engaging learning experiences. It emphasizes moral values, tolerance, and the memorization of short Quranic surahs, using simplified language and age-appropriate teaching methods to ensure understanding and meaningful participation in the learning process.
Social Studies Curriculum
For Arab and Non-Arab Students:

The curriculum aims to foster a strong sense of pride in the UAE’s rich cultural heritage while promoting the values of citizenship, tolerance, and national identity. Through observation and inquiry, Arab and non-Arab students gain a comprehensive understanding of the UAE’s history and culture.

children.text: SAIS - Dubai combines academic excellence with innovation, leadership development, and a strong commitment to holistic education. The campus is dedicated to preparing students for success through a values-driven American curriculum that promotes confidence, creativity, and lifelong learning.

Students benefit from comprehensive programs in STEM, athletics, arts, music, and languages. As a STEM.org accredited school, SAIS - Dubai places a strong emphasis on innovation, leadership, multilingual development, and meaningful extracurricular engagement that extends learning beyond the classroom.

children.text: Education at SAIS - Dubai is built on strong partnerships between students, families, and staff. Through a culture of trust, collaboration, and shared purpose, students are supported academically, socially, and emotionally while developing the resilience, confidence, and values needed to thrive.
The campus is fully accredited by NEASC and Cognia and is an authorized College Board testing center, reflecting its commitment to maintaining high international standards.

Student achievement spans academics, STEM, sports, literacy, and community engagement, and includes top placements in numerous high-profile competitions ranging from the AUS Sharakah Physics Open Day to the Abu Dhabi University AI Programming Competition.
